questions.q: Mock 1 · Q2. Domain of f(x) = 1/(x − 5) is
questions.why: The function 1/(x − 5) is undefined when x − 5 = 0, i.e. x = 5. So the domain is all real numbers except 5.

questions.q: Mock 1 · Q3. sin 120° equals
questions.why: sin 120° = sin(180° − 60°) = sin 60° = √3/2. Sine is positive in the second quadrant.

questions.q: Mock 1 · Q4. (1 + i)/(1 − i) equals
Mock 1 · Q5. Solution of 3 − 2x ≤ 9 is
questions.why: 3 − 2x ≤ 9 gives −2x ≤ 6. Dividing by −2 reverses the inequality, so x ≥ −3.

questions.q: Mock 1 · Q6. Number of ways to arrange the letters of 'LEVEL' is
questions.why: LEVEL has 5 letters with L twice and E twice. Arrangements = 5!/(2! 2!) = 120/4 = 30.

questions.q: Mock 1 · Q7. Coefficient of x⁴ in (1 + 2x)⁶ is
questions.why: The x⁴ term is ⁶C₄(2x)⁴ = 15 × 16x⁴ = 240x⁴, so the coefficient is 240.

questions.q: Mock 1 · Q8. The sum of the infinite G.P. 6 + 2 + 2/3 + … is
questions.why: This is a G.P. with a = 6 and r = 1/3, so the sum to infinity is 6/(1 − 1/3) = 6/(2/3) = 9.

questions.q: Mock 1 · Q9. If 3 tan x = 4 with x acute, sin 2x =
questions.why: 3 tan x = 4 gives tan x = 4/3, a 3-4-5 triangle, so sin x = 4/5 and cos x = 3/5. Then sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x = 2 × 4/5 × 3/5 = 24/25.

questions.q: Mock 1 · Q10. The number of 5-card hands with at least one ace from a 52-card deck is
questions.why: Hands with at least one ace = all hands − hands with no ace = ⁵²C₅ − ⁴⁸C₅. The other options undercount or count every hand.

questions.q: Mock 2 · Q1. Slope of 4x − 2y + 7 = 0 is
questions.why: The slope of Ax + By + C = 0 is −A/B = −4/(−2) = 2.

questions.q: Mock 2 · Q2. Centre of x² + y² − 10x + 4y − 7 = 0 is
questions.why: For x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 the centre is (−g, −f). Here 2g = −10 and 2f = 4, so g = −5, f = 2 and the centre is (5, −2).

questions.q: Mock 2 · Q3. d/dx (x³ sin x) is
questions.why: By the product rule, d/dx (x³ sin x) = 3x² sin x + x³ cos x.

questions.q: Mock 2 · Q4. lim (x→0) sin 7x / 2x is
questions.why: sin 7x/2x = (7/2)(sin 7x/7x). Since sin u/u → 1, the limit is 7/2.

questions.q: Mock 2 · Q5. Distance between (1, −2, 3) and (3, 0, 4) is
Mock 2 · Q6. Eccentricity of x²/9 + y²/5 = 1 is
questions.why: For x²/9 + y²/5 = 1, a² = 9 and b² = 5, so c² = 9 − 5 = 4 and c = 2. Eccentricity e = c/a = 2/3.

questions.q: Mock 2 · Q7. Variance of 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 is
questions.why: The mean is 6. Squared deviations are 16, 4, 0, 4, 16, which sum to 40. Variance = 40/5 = 8.

questions.q: Mock 2 · Q8. Two dice are thrown. P(doublet) is
questions.why: A doublet means both dice show the same number: (1,1), …, (6,6), which is 6 of the 36 outcomes. P = 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.q: Mock 2 · Q9. Equation of the parabola with focus (0, 4) and directrix y = −4 is
questions.why: A focus (0, a) with a directrix y = −a gives a = 4, and the parabola opens upward: x² = 4ay = 16y.

questions.q: Mock 2 · Q10. The derivative of (sin x + cos x)/(sin x − cos x) is
questions.why: Numerator: (cos − sin)(sin − cos) − (sin + cos)(cos + sin) = −(sin − cos)² − (sin + cos)² = −2.

courses.title: Ch 3 · Yoga
courses.summary: Meaning, aims and Ashtanga yoga, asanas and their benefits, pranayama and the shatkarmas.

scenes.text: Tanvi practises ten minutes of yoga each morning before board preparation.
She notices she sleeps better and concentrates longer.

steps.title: Meaning and aims
steps.body:
The word *yoga* comes from the Sanskrit root **yuj**, meaning to join or unite. Aims: physical health, mental balance, emotional stability and spiritual growth; union of individual self with the universal.

Patanjali's **Ashtanga yoga** (eight limbs): **Yama** (restraints), **Niyama** (observances), **Asana** (posture), **Pranayama** (breath control), **Pratyahara** (withdrawal of senses), **Dharana** (concentration), **Dhyana** (meditation), **Samadhi** (absorption).

steps.title: Solved example · classify
steps.body: Truthfulness (satya) → Yama. Cleanliness (shaucha) → Niyama. Sitting steadily in Sukhasana → Asana. Counting breaths in Nadi Shodhana → Pranayama. Fixing the mind on a candle flame → Dharana.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Reordering the limbs: the sequence is fixed.
- Reducing yoga to exercise only.

steps.title: Selected asanas
steps.body:
- **Tadasana** (mountain): posture, height gain, balance.
- **Vrikshasana** (tree): balance and concentration.
- **Bhujangasana** (cobra): strengthens back and spine; avoid in pregnancy, hernia, ulcers.
- **Dhanurasana** (bow): spine flexibility; avoid with hernia/hypertension.
- **Paschimottanasana** (seated forward bend): hamstring flexibility; avoid in slipped disc.
- **Vajrasana:** only asana usable after meals; aids digestion.
- **Shavasana:** relaxation.
Principles: empty stomach, gradual practice, listen to the body, learn from a trained teacher.

steps.title: Solved example
steps.body: A student with a lower-back problem asks about forward bends. Answer: avoid deep Paschimottanasana until a doctor or trained teacher advises; choose gentle, supervised alternatives.

steps.title: Safety
steps.body: General education, not medical advice. Stop if there is pain; see a doctor for medical conditions.

steps.title: Concepts
steps.body:
**Pranayama** = regulation of breath: **Puraka** (inhalation), **Kumbhaka** (retention), **Rechaka** (exhalation).
Types: Anuloma-Viloma/Nadi Shodhana, Kapalbhati (also a kriya), Ujjayi, Bhramari, Sheetali.
**Shatkarma** (six cleansing kriyas): Neti, Dhauti, Nauli, Basti, Kapalbhati, Trataka.
Precautions: learn under a trained teacher; avoid forceful breathing with heart disease, hypertension, pregnancy or recent surgery unless advised.

steps.title: Concepts
steps.body:
- **Physical fitness:** capacity to carry out daily tasks with vigour and still have energy for leisure and emergencies.
- **Wellness:** a state of optimal wellbeing — **physical, emotional, social, intellectual, spiritual, occupational, environmental** dimensions.
- **Health-related components:** cardiorespiratory endurance, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility, body composition.
- **Skill-related components:** speed, agility, balance, coordination, power, reaction time.

steps.title: Solved example
steps.body: Sort: a 1500 m run → cardiorespiratory endurance; touching toes → flexibility; a sprint start → reaction time; a vertical jump → power.

steps.title: Common mistake
steps.body: Treating wellness as absence of disease; it is active balance across dimensions.

scenes.text: The school nurse measures height and weight for every student.

steps.title: BMI
steps.body:
**BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height² (m²)**.
Adult WHO categories: <18.5 underweight; 18.5–24.9 normal; 25–29.9 overweight; ≥30 obese. For adolescents BMI is judged against age- and sex-specific percentile charts, so adult cut-offs do not directly apply. BMI does not separate muscle from fat.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body: Weight 60 kg, height 1.6 m: BMI = 60 ÷ (1.6 × 1.6) = 60 ÷ 2.56 = **23.4** → normal range (adult).

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body: Weight 81 kg, height 1.8 m: 81 ÷ 3.24 = **25.0** → overweight threshold.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Using height in cm.
- Forgetting to square.
- Judging teenagers by adult cut-offs; consult a doctor for interpretation.

Healthy lifestyle: balanced diet, activity, 8–10 hours sleep for teens, limiting screens and avoiding tobacco, alcohol, drugs, stress management.

courses.title: Ch 7 · Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology in Sports

scenes.text: A sprinter's hamstrings pull the leg back while quadriceps drive it forward.

steps.title: Concepts
steps.body:
- Adult skeleton: **206 bones**; functions: support, protection, movement, blood-cell production, mineral storage.
- **Joints:** fixed, slightly movable, freely movable (ball-and-socket at hip/shoulder, hinge at elbow/knee, pivot at neck).
- **Muscle types:** skeletal (voluntary, striated), cardiac (involuntary, striated), smooth (involuntary).
- **Fibre types:** slow-twitch (type I, endurance), fast-twitch (type II, power).
- Muscles work in pairs: **agonist** and **antagonist** (biceps/triceps).

steps.title: Solved example
steps.body: Marathon runner: higher proportion of slow-twitch fibres; sprinter: more fast-twitch fibres. Biceps contracts (agonist) while triceps relaxes (antagonist) during elbow flexion.

steps.title: Common mistake
steps.body: Calling cardiac muscle voluntary or non-striated.

scenes.text: After a run, Isha counts 30 beats in 15 seconds.

steps.title: Concepts
steps.body:
- Heart has four chambers; right side pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs, left side pumps oxygenated blood to the body.
- **Stroke volume (SV):** blood pumped per beat. **Cardiac output (Q) = heart rate × stroke volume.**
- Resting adult heart rate about 60–100 beats/min; trained athletes may be lower (athlete's heart/bradycardia).
- Estimated maximum heart rate ≈ **220 − age** (rough guide).

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body: 30 beats in 15 s → 30 × 4 = **120 beats/min**.

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body: Heart rate 72 beats/min, stroke volume 70 mL: Q = 72 × 70 = 5040 mL/min = **5.04 L/min**.

steps.title: Solved example 3
steps.body: Age 16 → estimated max HR = 220 − 16 = 204. 60% = 122.4 and 80% = 163.2, so the aerobic training zone is about 122–163 beats/min.

steps.title: Common mistake
steps.body: Treating 220 − age as exact; individuals differ.

steps.title: Concepts
steps.body:
- Respiration: nose → pharynx → larynx → trachea → bronchi → alveoli (gas exchange).
- Lung volumes: **tidal volume** (about 500 mL at rest), **vital capacity** (maximum air exhaled after maximum inhalation), **residual volume** (air remaining).
- Respiratory rate at rest about 12–20 breaths/min.
- **Effects of regular exercise:** stronger heart (larger stroke volume, lower resting HR), improved lung capacity and oxygen uptake (VO₂ max), stronger bones and muscles, better mood and sleep, better blood fats.
- Immediate effects: higher HR, breathing rate, blood pressure, body temperature.

steps.title: Solved example
steps.body: Breaths: 14 per minute × tidal volume 500 mL = **7000 mL/min** (minute ventilation) at rest.

steps.title: Remember
steps.body: VO₂ max = maximum oxygen the body can use per minute; trained athletes have higher values.

courses.title: Ch 10 · Training and Doping in Sports
courses.summary: Sports training principles, load, warm-up, conditioning, and doping with its health and ethical consequences.
outcomes: Define training and list its principles
Explain overload, specificity and progression
Plan warm-up and cool-down

courses.guardianNote: Discusses doping in sport factually and ethically; the aim is to explain why banned substances are harmful and unfair. It does not give use instructions.

scenes.text: Dev lifted the same weight for months and stopped improving.
His coach added progressive overload and recovery days.

steps.title: Concepts
steps.body:
**Sports training:** systematic, planned preparation to improve performance.
Principles: **overload** (stress above normal), **progression** (gradual increase), **specificity** (match the sport), **individualisation**, **reversibility** (detraining), **recovery/rest**, **variety**.
Load = intensity × volume. Periodisation: preparatory, competitive and transition periods.
**Warm-up** raises temperature, reduces injury and improves performance; **cool-down** aids recovery.

steps.title: Solved example
steps.body: A runner covers 20 km per week and increases by 10% weekly: week 2 = 22 km; week 3 = 24.2 km. This is **progressive overload**; adding rest every fourth week supports recovery.

steps.title: Common mistake
steps.body: Believing more training is always better; without recovery performance drops (overtraining).

steps.title: Methods
steps.body:
- **Endurance:** continuous running, interval training, fartlek.
- **Strength:** weight training, isometric, isotonic and circuit training.
- **Speed:** acceleration runs, repetition runs.
- **Flexibility:** static, dynamic and PNF stretching.
- **Coordination/agility:** drills, ladder work.
Note: young athletes should avoid heavy loading without supervision.

steps.title: Solved example
steps.body: **Circuit training** with 6 stations × 40 s work + 20 s rest = 6 min per round; 3 rounds = **18 min** total.

scenes.text: An athlete is banned after a test finds a prohibited substance.
The medals are returned and the athlete's career is damaged.

steps.title: Concepts
steps.body:
**Doping** is the use of prohibited substances or methods to improve performance artificially. Rules come from the **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)**, established in 1999, and the WADA Code with its Prohibited List; in India the **National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA)** conducts testing and education.
- Categories include anabolic agents, stimulants, diuretics/masking agents, hormones and blood doping.
- **Harms:** serious health risks (heart, liver, hormonal problems), unfair advantage, bans and loss of reputation.
- Athletes must check medicines before use (use the Therapeutic Use Exemption process where a medical need exists) and avoid unverified supplements.
- Education, testing, sanctions and fair play culture are the remedies.

steps.title: Solved example
steps.body: Q: An athlete takes a cold medicine without checking. Result: it contains a prohibited stimulant → possible violation. Lesson: check each medicine against the Prohibited List and consult a doctor and NADA resources.

steps.title: Common mistake
